title: Platform systems & services playbook — how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki (2026 Q4)
author: Liam Chen
summary: Central playbook for platform engineering: systems & services guidance, standard how-tos for dashboards and alerts, canonical runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings, and the near-term roadmap. This doc is the team wiki canonical reference for Q4 2026 operations and handoffs.
content:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single, opinionated reference for platform engineering (systems & services) that consolidates operational how-tos, dashboard/alert standards, runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings, and the next 6-12 month roadmap.
- Reduce cognitive load during incidents by ensuring runbooks, dashboards, and ownership information are discoverable and actionable.

Scope
- Applies to all platform-managed services: control plane APIs, routing/proxy, job scheduler, autoscaler, metric collectors, logging, tracing, and core dashboards used by oncall.
- Does NOT replace service-specific design docs; links to service ADRs and design pages are provided in related_pages.

Primary contacts / ownership
- Platform lead: Marcus Lee (eng-platform) — overall playbook stewardship.
- Oncall / SRE rotation: eng-sre (primary escalation).
- Runbook owners: each service team owns their service-specific runbooks; platform team maintains canonical platform runbooks in this doc.
- Slack channel: #eng-platform-oncall (pager duty hooks: Redwood-Platform-Pager).

Standards & Conventions
- Dashboards: Grafana is canonical. Panels should follow the standard naming: <service> / <endpoint> / <metric>. Use data source Prometheus.
- Alerts: use Prometheus Alertmanager with PagerDuty integration. Every alert must include: summary, severity (page|ticket|info), runbook link, owner.
- Runbooks: numbered steps (detect → mitigate → restore → postmortem), clearly labeled impact levels, TL;DR, and rollback steps if applicable.
- Metrics naming: use snake_case; labels must include service, cluster, region, and model (when applicable for inference).

Key SLOs (platform-level)
- API availability: 99.95% monthly for Redwood API control-plane endpoints.
- Inference request success rate: 99.9% monthly (measured as 2xx responses for hosted/dedicated control plane).
- Latency targets (observability panels configured to these): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 900ms for control-plane RPCs (these are soft targets; model inference p99 will vary by model and is tracked on per-model dashboards).

Dashboards & Alerts (how-to + recommended panels)

Grafana dashboard naming and panels (recommended canonical panels)
1) Platform Overview (dashboard id: platform-overview)
   - Total requests / min (sum by service)
   - 5xx rate (service, 1m and 5m windows)
   - Error budget consumption (per-service monthly)
   - CPU / Memory / GPU utilization (per-cluster, per-node-pool)
   - LB queue length, connection counts, and healthy backend %

2) Control Plane — API (dashboard id: cp-api)
   - P50/P95/P99 latency (Prometheus histogram_quantile on request_duration_seconds_bucket)
   - Request rate by endpoint (top endpoints by TPS)
   - 4xx/5xx by endpoint, with recent traces linked
   - DB connection pool usage and slow queries (if applicable)

3) Serving Runtime — Inference (dashboard id: serving-runtime)
   - Tokens/sec and requests/sec per GPU pool
   - Model-level tail latency (p95/p99) and KV-cache hit rate
   - Batch sizes, batching latency, and queue length per model variant
   - GPU memory fragmentation & utilization by node

4) Autoscaler & Jobs (dashboard id: autoscaler)
   - Pending pods / backoff rate / scaling events over time
   - Scale decisions with latency at decision time

Example queries (Prometheus / Grafana)
- P95 latency (Prometheus expression): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint, service))
- 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="control_plane"}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control_plane"}[5m])) by (service)

Alerting guidelines and common alerts
- Alert format: ALERT <alert_name>
  - severity: page | ticket | info
  - runbook: link to this doc section or service runbook
  - owner: team/service name

Critical (pager) alerts (examples)
- control_plane_5xx_spike (severity=page): if 5xx_rate(service) > 1% for 5m and absolute 5xx > 10 req/min — Page oncall.
- api_latency_p99_degradation (severity=page): if p99 latency > 2x baseline for 10m — Page oncall.
- gpu_pool_utilization_high (severity=page): if GPU idle < 5% and pending queue > 20 for 10m — Page capacity SRE.
- kafka_consumer_lag_critical (severity=page): if consumer_lag > 10k for 5m — Page streaming team.

Ticket (non-blocking) alerts
- storage_low_warn (severity=ticket): disk_used_percent > 80% for 24h — create ticket.
- config_diff_detected (severity=ticket): infra drift detected by sentinel — notify infra owners.

Runbooks — canonical platform runbooks (detect → mitigate → restore → postmortem)

1) High 5xx rate on control plane (runbook link: this doc / section)
- Detect: alert control_plane_5xx_spike fires; confirm via Grafana and recent traces (Tempo).
- Mitigate (TL;DR): divert traffic to alternate region/model variants, scale control-plane replicas, enable degraded mode (read-only) for non-essential endpoints.
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty alert.
  2. Open incident channel #inc-{alertid}-platform in Slack using template (see appendix).
  3. Confirm scope: which endpoints, models, and clients affected.
  4. If error origin is upstream DB: follow DB failover runbook. If origin is runtime (OOMs / overloaded GPUs): scale GPU pool or disable low-priority model variants.
  5. Apply short-term mitigations: scale control-plane replicas (kubectl scale deployment cp-api --replicas=N), rollback recent deploy if correlated within 15min.
  6. Monitor for recovery for 10m windows; if not recovered escalate to engineering manager and platform lead.
- Restore: ensure normal 5xx rate and latency for 30m, then close incident.
- Postmortem: owner assigns postmortem within 48h, with timeline, root cause, corrective actions and RCA link to confluence.

2) GPU pool saturated / long queues for inference jobs
- Detect: gpu_pool_utilization_high fires and queue length > threshold; p95 latency increases and KV-cache hit ratio drops.
- Mitigate: enable reserve pool (burst capacity), move non-critical batches to lower-priority pool, temporarily disable large-batch scheduling.
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty alert.
  2. Report current pending queue, GPU utilization, and next autoscale decision time in incident channel.
  3. If autoscaler failed to spin up new nodes, check cloud quotas and events, then trigger manual node group increase.
  4. If model variant is causing unusually high resource use, take variant out of rotation (k8s: set pod annotation routing.disable=true) and re-route to compatible variant.
  5. Close incident after 2 successful stabilization windows (10m each).

3) Metrics/observability gap (missing dashboards / scrape failures)
- Detect: missing_series_detected alert, or significant drop in total metric ingestion.
- Mitigate: check Prometheus targets, scrape logs, restart prometheus if needed, switch read-only fallback Grafana to cached snapshots.
- Steps: standard diagnostics: prometheustsdb_check, disk space, connection to federation endpoints.

How-to: Create a new dashboard panel (quick guide)
1. Name convention: <service> — <component> — <metric>. Avoid long titles.
2. Use Prometheus datasource. Select metric, apply labels {service="<svc>", cluster="<cluster>"}.
3. Use range 1h and 5m resolution by default for oncall dashboards.
4. Add a short panel description with a link to the runbook and owner.
5. Add alert only if the metric has a clear remediation path. Otherwise mark panel as "observability only".

How-to: Add an alert to Alertmanager
1. Create alert rule in prometheus/rules/ with fields: expr, for, labels (severity, owner), annotations (runbook, summary).
2. Run rule-lint (scripts/check-alerts.sh) to ensure format.
3. Submit PR targeting infra-ops; include test plan (local prom test, unit tests).
4. After merge, monitor for false positives for 48h.

Retrospective summary (last major incidents)
- Incident: Q3 2026 API outage (2026-08-18)
  - Root cause: memory leak in control-plane metrics collector after a rolling deploy.
  - Actions: introduced stricter memory limits and liveness probes; added incremental rollout policy for metrics-collector (50% canary for 30m) — owner: eng-platform — completed 2026-09-10.
  - Learnings: increase canary duration for stateful components; require benchmark with synthetic traffic before global rollout.

- Incident: Q2 2026 GPU saturation on Black Friday test (2026-06-24)
  - Root cause: autoscaler tuning too conservative for burst workloads.
  - Actions: implement predictive scaling policy, increase GPU reserve pool, and add pre-warming runbook for scheduled large tests — owner: eng-infra — planned Q1 2027.

Action items from retrospectives (owner and ETA)
- A1: Add chaos tests for metrics collector memory pressure — owner: eng-platform — ETA 2026-12-15.
- A2: Document canary rollout checklist for stateful services — owner: eng-platform — ETA 2026-11-30.
- A3: Implement predictive autoscaling for GPU pools (prototype) — owner: eng-infra — ETA 2027-02-28.

Roadmap (near-term priorities, Q4 2026 — Q2 2027)
- Q4 2026:
  - Canonicalize dashboards and migrate key panels to templated dashboards (owner: eng-platform)
  - Implement alert severity overhaul (reduce noisy pages) (owner: eng-sre)
  - Deliver runbook automation: incident channel templates and postmortem skeletons (owner: eng-platform)
- Q1 2027:
  - Predictive GPU autoscaler prototype and field test (owner: eng-infra + eng-serving-runtime)
  - Improved per-model observability (per-model cost/latency dashboards) (owner: applied-ml-and-evals)
- Q2 2027:
  - Autoscaler policy rollout and SLA updates for Dedicated customers (owner: product + eng-platform)

Team wiki & onboarding notes (quick links and checklist)
- Oncall checklist (first 15 minutes): acknowledge alert, gather scope, post in incident channel, begin mitigations or triage.
- Account setup: link to Grafana, PagerDuty, Slack.
- Where to find runbooks: this page (bookmark) + service-specific runbooks under /confluence/eng-platform/<service-name>.
- New hire 1-week tasks: read SLOs, run through mock incident game-day, create one dashboard panel, contribute to runbook update.

Appendices
A. Incident channel templates
- Use template: [INCIDENT START]
  - Title: <short title>
  - Impact: <short impact statement>
  - Affects: services, regions, customers
  - Actions in progress: <list>
  - Owner: <oncall name>
  - Link to runbook: <link>
  - [INCIDENT END]

B. Contact & escalation matrix
- PagerDuty: Redwood-Platform-Pager (primary)
- Slack: #eng-platform-oncall (primary comms)
- Engineering manager escalation: Marcus Lee (phone + calendar)
- Platform lead: Marcus Lee (marcus@redwood.example.com)

C. Suggested dashboard template (panels to clone)
- Left column: Availability / Latency / Error rate
- Middle column: Capacity (CPU/GPU/Memory) and queue length
- Right column: Traces and recent deploys (linked)

D. Playbook change process
1. Propose change by editing this page and creating a PR against confluence-source repo.
2. Tag reviewers (eng-platform, eng-sre) and include a roll-back plan for any alerting changes.
3. After merge, monitor the change for 7 days and add retrospective note if the change impacted oncall noise.

Notes & references
- Link to SRE SLA doc: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
